rationale: Identity copy (expected=[0,1]) using both slots in parallel. Both reads are issued before a single blocking wait_reads, so after it no pending reads remain and both slots are initialized at every reachable state, making publish/acquire/write valid under any DMA completion order (reads are non-FIFO but wait_reads waits for the whole queue). Both writes target distinct destinations from distinct acquired slots; a single blocking wait_writes guarantees no pending transfers before either release, so release is valid regardless of write completion order. Final state: pc=end, no pending transfers, all slots free, dst0 origin 0 and dst1 origin 1 as required. Minimality: publish requires an initialized value and release requires no pending transfer, so at least one wait_reads and one wait_writes are unavoidable; with waits minimized to 2, each page needs reserve+read+publish+acquire+write and each reserved slot needs release, giving 12+2=14 commands, which is the minimum. Peak live slots is 2, the minimum possible for a 2-wait program, since overlapping both copies behind shared waits requires both slots reserved simultaneously (a peak-1 serial schedule would need 4 waits, losing on the lexicographically primary criterion).
